claim_evidence_type_note: flagquantum.runtime.audit.vocabulary.CLAIM_EVIDENCE_TYPES is a closed set with no cross-framework comparison member, so this payload declares 'unknown' rather than inventing a term. comparison_class carries the real meaning. The benchmark audit accepts the payload without promoting it.
scalability_blockers: One GPU was used and one logical workload ran on it. No workload was partitioned across ranks, so no capacity-expansion statement follows from this artifact.

The two sides do not execute the same schedule. The CUDA-Q side issues one host-side call per gradient evaluation while the FlagQuantum side calls one fused compiled program, so a gradient-path ratio measures call structure as well as numeric throughput.
source_revision_note: The runtime images carry no git binary, so each probe recorded source_identity.commit as null. The link from payload to source is the recorded runner_sha256, which was read back with sha256sum inside each container and matches this revision's file byte for byte.

cross_host_spread.note: Same probe, same revision, same CUDA-Q release, two different hosts and two different base images. This is the reproducibility check: a conclusion that does not survive it is a measurement of one machine.

methodology.flagquantum_jit: on except where a case disables it
methodology.timing: Wall clock around the whole value-and-gradient call, after warmup, averaged over the timed iterations. Host-side structure is part of what is measured on both sides.
methodology.precision_alignment: Every case is reported only when both sides agree on the loss and, where a gradient ran, on the gradient. A case that failed the tolerance would be recorded as a failure rather than dropped.

protocol_sensitivity.note: Recorded because the same 18-wire gradient invocation produced 72.3 ms in an earlier capture and 39.2 ms in this one. Rather than choose between them, the warmup count was swept with the iteration count fixed.
protocol_sensitivity.consequence: The forward-only conclusion is insensitive to warmup: the 22-wire case moves 0.1% between one and three warmups, so the widening gap it shows is a property of the two implementations. The 18-wire gradient ratio is not settled by this protocol: it rises monotonically with warmup, from 13.6x at one warmup to 16.3x at five, so a single digit must not be quoted for it. An earlier capture of the same configuration reported 7.9x, and that number is withdrawn as an under-warmed reading rather than reproduced.

withdrawn.reason: The same invocation reads 39.2 ms at the recorded protocol and 32.6 ms at five warmups. The 72.3 ms that produced 7.9x was a cold reading, not a steady state.
